WIDDIN, May 11.


MY LORD! it was the end of April that the
Russians withdrew from before Giurdzeow. Musta-
pha Bailaw was acquainted with this retreat
only at break of day he found in their camp
the annexed letter, addressed to this Bailaw by
N. Rodolinlin.


General Michelson has fallen back with his
forces beyond the Siret, leaving only towards
Bucharest rear guard of light troops, posted
behind Argis and Dombowitz.


All communication is forbidden to the inhab-
itants that these retrograde steps may not be
known. It is difficult to form an idea of the
chagrin of the partisans of the Russians in Wal-
achia. Several of the principal Boyards and
of the Greek clergy are justly accused of having
favoured the Russians. The others said to them,
"in refusing to take arms, as long as the Em-
peror Napoleon will remain in Poland, and that
you will be so feeble, you cannot inspire us with
any confidence."


The Walachians who have taken the part
of the Russians, fly away on all sides. Many
have made bitter reproaches to Michelson.
"Why they have said to him, did you
come to disturb us. We have taken up arms
upon the faith of your Emperor, and you aban-
don us you promised us every day new suc-
cours, and none have arrived You however
knew that you were not able to maintain your
ground with the few troops which you had here.
why then did you excite us on to deliver us up
to an enemy, who do not pardon to expose us
to the vengeance of our irritated sovereign
Unfortunate that we are, we have forgotten the
advice of our fathers. They had told us that
you had acted thus many times that we can
never expect to be in your hands but instruments
which are sacrificed for the least convenience.
Happy those who have remained faithful and ob-
edient."


The Turkish forces increase upon the Danube.
Mustapha Bailaw has caused to march from s
to 5000 men, to reduce Philippopoli, where a
rebellion has arisen against his authority.


The Grand Vizier is marching with the main
body of his army he advances towards Baba
dag. His van guard is commanded by Ali b.
Bailaw, (Cercazy) who has arrived at Irmail.
The left of the army of the grand Vizier is at Kir-
ichowa and SiliitIia. This position of the of
oman army turns General Michelson, who has
not only done well in evacuating Walachia,
but who will soon be obliged to evacuate Beta-
rabia.


The check which the Russians have sustained
before FINAL, previous to the arrival of the
Grand Vizier, leaves sufficient to conjecture
whether they are able to resist him. The tak-
ing of Ismail is the principal point of their plan.
The numerous checks they have sustained with
in three months, before that place, are of great
consequence to the Porte who will derive great
advantages from them. The army of Michel-
son is of a number inferior to 60 600 men. He
has not found in Walachia all the encouragement
and assistance which he expected. The succes-
ses of the French army have kept the greatest
number under the obedience of the Porte.


The wretched Walachians are not the only
ones to be pitied, the only ones abandoned by
Russia. The Servians who remained quiet in
under the cover of an armistice, have run to arms
by their mitigation they repaired to the height
parallel with the Danube. They had posted in
the principal island of that river, between the
mouths of the Timock and Orgaheka, about
four hundred men, to make themselves masters
of that passage, and were determined to wait for
the Russians, who failed to go to the rendez-
vous. These wretches have been the victims of
their confidence. Being killed a great many
drowned themselves, & hardly thirty could save
themselves by swimming. Servia finds herself at
attacked at the same time by all the B flaws, and
this objectionable insurrection is carried on
by the Russians, who have faced
them. This blind confidence in the lies of
Russia, is for her the source of great misfor-
tune.


The Bailaw of Widen began his march the
9th May towards Nagodiu, to pursue his adj-
vantages over the Sergans. He has ordered a
small battalion fort to be erected to secure
the island which is occupied by his last detachment.


The Porte has ordered to repair the place of
Oriowa, very important position.


p. S. At the moment of closing my letter, I
received one from Mons. Lamarre, who writes
to me from Rudgebuck that Prince Ara has
just gained a new advantage on the lower Da-
nube.


Accept, my Lord, &c.


(Signed) The Adjutant Commandant,
MERIAGE.
